question.problem:
Simplify $tanh\,(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)$ using the definition of the hyperbolic tangent.

$tanh\,(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=$

| {{field-1}} |
| --- |
| ${x}^{3}+1$ |
question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{tanh}⁡x$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x & =\frac{{e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}}{{e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x}-1}{{e}^{2x}+1} \\  & =\frac{1-{e}^{-2x}}{1+{e}^{-2x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the second definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}tanh\,(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) & =\frac{{e}^{2(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}-1}{{e}^{2(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3\operatorname{ln}⁡x}-1}{{e}^{3\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{3}}-1}{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{3}}+1} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}-1}{{x}^{3}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$
